title: Redwood Private VPC security architecture deep dive with Starling Bank
summary: Redwood ran a deep dive on Private VPC deployment topology, focusing on network isolation, ingress/egress controls, firewalling, KMS/HSM key management, audit logs & SIEM integration, and SSO/RBAC. Starling has strict data residency and egress restrictions; discussed options: PrivateLink with interface endpoints, AWS Direct Connect/Transit GW peering, or on-prem package. Agreed next steps: share SOC2 and architecture diagrams, propose a POC window, and schedule follow-up for Okta SCIM mapping.
next_steps: Maya Patel: send SOC 2 report, ISO gap notes, and high-level network diagram by 2026-03-08
Ethan Liu: prepare proposed VPC peering/PrivateLink + Transit GW diagram and hardened security group/NACL templates by 2026-03-10
Priya Desai: provide list of required IP ranges and egress blocklist by 2026-03-09

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-05 15:00 ET
Duration: 65 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Oliver Grant, Priya Desai, Liam O'Connor (Starling)

Summary (auto): Redwood and Starling run through private VPC deployment and security controls; customer to validate IP/egress lists and decide on customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed KMS.

Topics: SOC 2 / ISO questions, RBAC/SSO integration (Okta), audit logging & SIEM, data residency, KMS/HSM, VPC isolation, ingress/egress, firewalling, NAT/egress proxies, PrivateLink/Direct Connect options.

Transcript (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect):
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick intros then jump into the private vpc arch, i'm maya redwood ae, with ethan who is our platform se.
[00:22] Oliver: thanks, i'm oliver head of cloud at starling, priya's our security architect and liam does ops, we have pretty tight controls for egress and data residency.
[00:35] Ethan: great, quick agenda: network isolation (ingress/egress), identity (sso/rbac), audit logs + siem, encryption and kms/hsm, then q&a and next steps. sound good?
[00:50] Priya: yes, also want to cover legal requirements around key custody and whether model logs leave our environment.
[01:05] Maya: totally, we'll start with topology. so high-level we offer a private control plane + runtime that can be deployed in customer VPCs or on-prem. for aws customers common patterns are PrivateLink endpoints or Transit Gateway peering with dedicated subnets.
[01:30] Oliver: ok, what's the difference in terms of ingress? does traffic go over internet or via privatelink?
[01:38] Ethan: with PrivateLink you get ENIs and endpoint services in your VPC; traffic stays inside aws backbone. no public internet path to the runtime. with Direct Connect or DX/Transit you can also route to our managed VPCs if you prefer. we also support air-gapped on-prem installs.
[02:05] Priya: how do you handle TLS termination? we require mutual tls for all control plane APIs.
[02:12] Ethan: we support mTLS end-to-end. TLS is terminated at your ALB or at the private endpoint depending on topology; we can use customer-provided certs and require client certs for service-to-service. sometimes certs are managed via ACM with private CA integration.
[02:36] Liam: if we go privatelink do you still need outbound egress from our subnets?
[02:42] Ethan: minimal. the runtime in your VPC handles model downloads from an internal S3-compatible store — we can either mirror model artifacts into your S3 bucket during onboarding or stage them in a customer-managed bucket. if you choose customer-managed S3, there is no egress to our buckets.
[03:10] Priya: we need to ensure no logs with pii are sent out. how do you handle audit logs and redaction?
[03:18] Maya: our logs can be configured — we export control plane and runtime logs to your CloudWatch/Datadog/Splunk endpoints. you can set filters to redact sensitive fields. we'll share the mapping of fields we collect.
[03:40] Priya: do you provide prescriptive retention policies for audit logs to meet our compliance?
[03:46] Ethan: yes, we can set retention on the customer side; additionally, we keep an internal audit trail for a limited period for platform health. SOC2/ISO docs specify retention and we can show the policy.
[04:05] Oliver: talk to me about key management. we require customer-managed keys for all production data at rest. can you integrate with our AWS KMS/HSM?
[04:15] Ethan: we support customer-managed CMKs in AWS KMS, and for HSM we support cloud HSM in a BYOK flow. keys can be restricted via key policies so only the runtime in your account can decrypt. we also support a bring-your-own-HSM model for on-prem.
[04:40] Priya: does redwood ever hold plaintext model outputs or keys?
[04:45] Maya: no, with private deployments keys remain in your control and plaintext output is processed within your VPC. for hosted options we encrypt at rest and in transit, and keys may be more managed by redwood — that's why many customers choose private for sensitive workloads.
[05:05] Liam: firewalling - what do you expect from our side for security groups and NACL?
[05:12] Ethan: we recommend least-priv SGs (only allow port 443 inbound for endpoints), restrict outbound to the minimal set of artifact endpoints (or none if using customer S3), and use NACLs to provide another layer. we can provide hardened templates.
[05:32] Priya: do you support egress whitelisting? we need to only allow specific IP ranges.
[05:37] Ethan: yes, we can operate with fixed egress ranges and provide those for firewall rules. if you require absolute zero egress we can do full artifact mirroring and block external egress.
[05:55] Priya: what about network monitoring and IDS?
[06:00] Maya: we integrate with CloudTrail, GuardDuty, and can forward flow logs to your SIEM. for on-prem we can connect to your existing IDS via syslog/SIEM forwarders.
[06:18] Oliver: on certification front, do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001?
[06:24] Maya: yes, SOC2 Type II for 2025 and ISO 27001 cert — we'll upload the packages. i'm sending those after the call.
[06:35] Priya: ok, on SSO we use okta, want scim provisioning and groups mapped to roles. how does your rbac work?
[06:42] Ethan: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. roles are mapped in our RBAC to least-privilege roles: admin, operator, auditor, app-only API keys. we can restrict token lifetimes and require mfa.
[07:05] Priya: can we disable long-lived api keys?
[07:09] Ethan: yes, tokens can be short-lived and rotated; we also integrate with your vault for secrets.
[07:18] Liam: audit log export — can we push audit events into our Splunk?
[07:22] Ethan: absolutely; we have a connector and can stream to HTTP/S or Kinesis Firehose. logs can include request/response metadata but we can redact content per policy.
[07:40] Priya: any concerns about multi-tenancy? we want strict tenant isolation at the network and storage layer.
[07:46] Maya: in private VPC deployments you get dedicated subnets and resources; storage is exclusive and network isolation is enforced. for hosted models we use strong tenant isolation but some customers with strict regs choose private.
[08:05] Oliver: what about model updates and software patches, how are they pushed?
[08:12] Ethan: for private we push runtime updates via your CI/CD pipeline or via out-of-band installers; patches can be scheduled with maintenance windows. model downloads are gated through signed artifacts and checksums.
[08:30] Priya: does your runtime require opening additional ports for health checks, metrics, etc?
[08:35] Ethan: typically just 443; metrics are pushed to your observability endpoints or scraped from within your VPC on a private port — we can keep that internal.
[08:50] Maya: okay switching to ingress patterns: two common options – PrivateLink endpoint services or customer-managed ALB with route to runtime in dedicated subnets. PrivateLink simplifies firewall rules since it's ENI-based.
[09:10] Priya: if we use PrivateLink, does it create cross-account ENIs into our VPC?
[09:15] Ethan: yes, it creates interface endpoints in your account. traffic stays in the aws backbone. endpoint policy can limit which principals can connect.
[09:30] Liam: are you using NAT gateways for outbound artifact pulls?
[09:34] Ethan: depends on setup; if you're allowing outbound then NAT is used. otherwise we mirror artifacts to your S3. we can also use VPC endpoints to keep traffic internal.
[09:50] Priya: wanted to confirm retention for audit logs to comply with our policy: 7 years for some events. is that supported?
[09:58] Ethan: for logs in your account you control retention; we'll document what events we emit and you can keep them per policy. internal platform retention is shorter but we can provide exports for long-term archival.
[10:20] Oliver: timeline wise we're targeting a pilot in Q2 if contracts and security ok.
[10:26] Maya: good, pilot is normal 4-6 weeks. ethan will propose a POC design.
[10:32] Ethan: i'll include a proposed networking template, SGs, NACLs and privatelink diagram.
[10:40] Priya: on keys – if we use customer-managed KMS, can we revoke access quickly? need key rotation and emergency revoke.
[10:47] Ethan: yes, using CMKs you control rotation and revoke. for HSM we can show key custody flows.
[10:58] Priya: do you log who accessed keys and when?
[11:02] Ethan: yes KMS has key usage logs in CloudTrail; we surface these and can link to our audit events as well.
[11:20] Oliver: any public docs for the on-prem installer?
[11:24] Maya: yes, we have a private-deploy repo; i'll share a readme link after call.
[11:34] Liam: what about internal service accounts – do they run with least privilege and can you show us evidence?
[11:40] Ethan: yes we can provide role definitions and an internal roles matrix. part of SOC2 evidence folder.
[11:55] Priya: network egress – can you guarantee IP ranges won't change mid-pilot? we need stable ranges for firewall rules.
[12:03] Ethan: we provide published egress ranges and a change policy; for private deploys ranges are controlled inside your account so change risk is low.
[12:20] Priya: for handling PII we want to enable tokenization at ingress if possible. supported?
[12:26] Ethan: we have pre-processing hooks and can integrate a lambda or sidecar to tokenize before it hits the runtime; that's typical.
[12:40] Maya: quick note - regarding legal and contract, our security addendum includes data residency, breach notification timelines, and audit rights.
[12:52] Priya: ok please send the addendum.
[13:00] Maya: noted, will include with soc docs.
[13:08] Oliver: ok any performance implications of privatelink vs dedicated peering?
[13:14] Ethan: both are low latency on aws backbone; peering via transit gw is good for high throughput. privatelink has some bandwidth considerations but usually fine for API traffic.
[13:30] Priya: about model caching inside our VPC: if we cache kv/llm context, is that stored encrypted?
[13:36] Ethan: yes cached items are encrypted at rest under your kms keys when in your account.
[13:45] Liam: change control - how do we coordinate patch windows?
[13:50] Ethan: we have maintenance windows and change notifications; for private we always schedule with ops.
[14:02] Priya: final question on PCI/regulated data — can you guarantee that cardholder data never leaves our VPC?
[14:09] Maya: yes if you run private deployment with mirrored artifacts and customer-managed s3 & kms, cardholder data can stay in your environment. we will document processing boundaries.
[14:30] Oliver: sounds good, thanks. let's recap next steps.
[14:36] Maya: recap: we'll send SOC2 + ISO packages, architecture diagrams, privatelink/transit gw templates, and a proposed poc plan. priya will share ip/egress blocklist and key custody requirements. set follow-up next week to align on POC scope.
[14:58] Priya: noted.
[15:05] Maya: thanks all, meeting adjourned.

Notes: occasional transcription errors (k s m -> kms, privatelink spelled private link in some lines). References: SOC2 package link: drive/Redwood/SOC2-2025.pdf, PrivateDeploy README: github.com/redwood/private-deploy, Networking diagram: drive/Redwood/diagrams/starling-vpc-arch-2026.png
